long_biography.plain_text:
Control of a major British retail group placed Salah Al-Fayed within House of Fraser's ownership structure. With Mohamed and Ali Fayed, he beneficially owned and controlled Al Fayed Investment and Trust, the vehicle that secured a majority holding in the retailer in 1985. The acquisition included Harrods and established the three brothers in British department-store ownership.

Al-Fayed served as a director of two companies connected to the Ritz Paris before resigning from both in 1994. By then he was running the family's business interests in Egypt, while Mohamed chaired Harrods. His position combined ownership through the shared holding company with an overseas managerial remit, distinct from the public chairmanship associated with his elder brother.
